title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI
research_question: How large are plausible medium-run macroeconomic productivity, wage and inequality effects of AI?

data.type: calibration from exposure and task-level productivity estimates

method.boundary: conditional projection, not causal aggregate estimate

findings.claim: Under the paper's exposure and task-cost assumptions, projected TFP gains over ten years are modest and below 0.53% after adjusting for hard-to-learn tasks.
Task-level gains for lower-skill workers do not by themselves imply reduced inequality; capital-labor income gaps may widen.
findings.locator: NBER version, abstract and inequality analysis

limitations: Calibration depends on exposure and cost-saving assumptions.
US-centered evidence; fast model change limits transportability.
